cancer_indication: HR+, HER2-negative metastatic breast cancer with activating PIK3CA mutations, in combination with fulvestrant after progression on endocrine therapy.
moa: Alpelisib is an oral, highly selective ATP-competitive inhibitor of the p110α catalytic subunit of class IA phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase (PIK3CA), blocking conversion of PIP2 to PIP3 and preventing downstream AKT/mTOR activation in PIK3CA-mutant breast cancer cells. In HR+ breast cancer, activating PIK3CA mutations drive PI3K-pathway hyperactivation and endocrine resistance, so PI3Kα inhibition reduces proliferative and survival signaling. By suppressing PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling and ER cross-talk, particularly when combined with ER antagonists such as fulvestrant, alpelisib induces G1 arrest and promotes apoptosis in PIK3CA-dependent, luminal tumors.

REACTOME_PI3K_AKT_ACTIVATION.description: PI3K–AKT signaling transduces growth factor and oncogenic cues through PIP3-dependent activation of AKT and downstream effectors, including mTOR, to promote cell proliferation and survival.
REACTOME_PI3K_AKT_ACTIVATION.interpretation: In PIK3CA-mutant HR+ breast cancer, this pathway is hyperactivated and drives endocrine resistance and tumor growth; alpelisib directly inhibits PI3Kα to shut down AKT/mTOR output in sensitive tumors.

REACTOME_MTOR_SIGNALLING.description: mTOR signaling integrates upstream inputs from PI3K/AKT to regulate protein synthesis, cell growth, and metabolism via effectors such as S6K and 4EBP1.
REACTOME_MTOR_SIGNALLING.interpretation: Downstream mTORC1 activity is initially suppressed by PI3Kα inhibition but becomes hyperactivated in acquired alpelisib resistance, where elevated phospho-S6K and phospho-4EBP1 sustain proliferation despite PI3K blockade.

REACTOME_SIGNALING_BY_ERBB2.description: ERBB2/HER2 signaling is a receptor tyrosine kinase pathway that activates PI3K/AKT and MAPK cascades in response to HER2 overexpression or amplification.
REACTOME_SIGNALING_BY_ERBB2.interpretation: In HER2+ PIK3CA-mutant breast cancers, ERBB2 signaling cooperates with PI3K activation and confers resistance to anti-HER2 therapy; combining alpelisib with HER2-targeted agents can overcome this in preclinical models.

REACTOME_ESR_MEDIATED_SIGNALING.description: ESR-mediated signaling reflects estrogen receptor (ER, ESR1)–driven transcriptional programs that regulate luminal differentiation, proliferation, and endocrine response in HR+ breast cancer.
REACTOME_ESR_MEDIATED_SIGNALING.interpretation: ER signaling is a dominant driver in HR+ disease; combining alpelisib with ER antagonists such as fulvestrant suppresses ER target gene expression and improves outcomes in PIK3CA-mutant tumors.

GOBP_INFLAMMATORY_RESPONSE.description: The inflammatory response gene program (e.g., GO:0006955) encompasses innate and adaptive immune signaling, including interferon and cytokine pathways.
GOBP_INFLAMMATORY_RESPONSE.interpretation: Immune and inflammatory gene sets, including interferon response signatures, are upregulated in alpelisib-resistant breast cancer models, suggesting inflammatory and immune programs accompany or facilitate escape from PI3K inhibition.

KEGG_GLYCOLYSIS_GLUCONEOGENESIS.description: Glycolysis/gluconeogenesis controls cellular glucose utilization and energy production through glycolytic enzymes and associated metabolic nodes.
KEGG_GLYCOLYSIS_GLUCONEOGENESIS.interpretation: PI3K activation promotes glycolysis, and alpelisib-resistant cells exhibit increased reliance on glucose metabolism; metabolic vulnerabilities in glycolysis become exploitable in resistant tumors.

KEGG_MAPK_SIGNALING_PATHWAY.description: MAPK signaling relays mitogenic stimuli via RAS–RAF–MEK–ERK to regulate cell proliferation, survival, and differentiation.
KEGG_MAPK_SIGNALING_PATHWAY.interpretation: Activation of MAPK/ERK signaling, including through RAS or FGFR1-driven pathways, acts as a bypass route that can diminish alpelisib sensitivity by sustaining growth signals independent of PI3K.

REACTOME_CELL_CYCLE.description: Cell cycle pathways orchestrate progression through G1, S, G2, and M phases, including cyclin/CDK control of G1–S transition.
REACTOME_CELL_CYCLE.interpretation: PI3K and ER signaling converge on cell-cycle regulators; alpelisib treatment leads to G1 arrest with reduced cyclin D1 and proliferation in sensitive HR+ breast cancer cells.

HALLMARK_APOPTOSIS.description: Apoptosis represents programmed cell death mediated by intrinsic and extrinsic pathways that eliminate damaged or stressed cells.
HALLMARK_APOPTOSIS.interpretation: When AKT-mediated survival signaling is suppressed by PI3Kα inhibition, pro-apoptotic programs are unleashed, contributing to tumor cell death in alpelisib-sensitive contexts.

STEIN_ESR1_TARGETS.description: ESR1 target gene sets capture transcriptional programs directly regulated by estrogen receptor alpha in luminal breast cancer.
STEIN_ESR1_TARGETS.interpretation: ESR1-driven transcription remains a key dependency in many PIK3CA-mutant, luminal tumors; ESR1 mutations and active ER signaling are associated with clinical benefit from alpelisib plus fulvestrant, which together suppress ER targets and PI3K output.

sensitivity_genes_up_annotations.interpretation: Activating PIK3CA mutations define the target population for alpelisib; in pivotal HR+/HER2− metastatic trials, the presence of a PIK3CA mutation was required and predictive of benefit, as alpelisib directly inhibits mutant PI3Kα in these tumors.

ESR1-mutant, ER-driven tumors remained clinically responsive when estrogen signaling was blocked with fulvestrant and PI3Kα was inhibited by alpelisib, indicating that active ER/ESR1 signaling in combination with effective ER blockade is associated with sensitivity.

resistance_genes_up_annotations.interpretation: High baseline activity of bypass pathways, including FGFR1 amplification, is linked to lower sensitivity to PI3K inhibition; FGFR1-driven MAPK/ERK signaling can maintain proliferative signaling and reduce alpelisib efficacy.

resistance_genes_down_annotations.interpretation: Loss of the negative regulator PTEN leads to unchecked PI3K signaling; PTEN loss is described as a mechanism that would confer resistance to alpelisib by reactivating PIP3 and downstream AKT despite PI3Kα inhibition.

notes: JSON derived strictly from the provided deep-research document on alpelisib in human breast cancer, focusing on PIK3CA-mutant HR+/HER2− disease and related pathway behavior; gene-level sensitivity and resistance assignments are limited to PIK3CA, ESR1, FGFR1, and PTEN where explicitly described.
